    Structured (Cornfield–Tukey / Satterthwaite) denominator construction

    structured_denominator.Rd

    Builds a pseudo-F denominator for a mixed-model term by *synthesising* mean squares in containment-lattice order, rather than by the unconstrained minimum-norm match used in [quasi_denominator()]. Given the expected mean squares (EMS) of a set of sources, each random source's variance component, and the observed mean squares, it peels the target EMS one variance component at a time from the top of the lattice down, using the source that directly estimates each component. On a clean balanced design this returns the exact single-source denominator; on a perturbed design (e.g. an unbalanced or covariate-containing mixed model) it returns the structured linear combination with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, matching the construction used by classical mixed-model software.

    structured_denominator(ems, mean_squares, dfs, leading, target, tol = 1e-08)

    Arguments

    ems

    Numeric matrix of EMS coefficients, one row per source (named) and one column per variance component (named). Entry `ems[i, j]` is the coefficient of component `j` in the expected mean square of source `i`.

    mean_squares

    Named numeric vector of observed mean squares, one per source (names matching `rownames(ems)`).

    dfs

    Named numeric vector of degrees of freedom, one per source.

    leading

    Named character vector mapping each *random* source to the variance component it directly estimates (e.g. `c(Residual = "residual", Site = "site")`); fixed sources are omitted or `NA`.

    target

    The source to test: the denominator is built to match its EMS with its own leading component removed. May instead be a named numeric target EMS vector.

    tol

    Numerical tolerance for treating coefficients as zero.

    Value

    A list with the denominator `weights` (named), its value, and its Satterthwaite `df`.

    Examples

    # A balanced two-level nested design: Site over Residual is exact.
ems <- rbind(Site = c(residual = 1, site = 4),
             Residual = c(residual = 1, site = 0))
structured_denominator(ems, c(Site = 3, Residual = 1), c(Site = 5, Residual = 40),
                       leading = c(Residual = "residual", Site = "site"),
                       target = "Site")
#> $weights
#> Residual 
#>        1 
#> 
#> $value
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $df
#> [1] 40
#>
